title: Count Good Triplets
signature: int countGoodTriplets(int[] arr, int a, int b, int c)
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 100 values there are fewer than 162,000 index triples, so checking every one is fast enough. The only refinement worth making is to test the first rule as soon as `i` and `j` are fixed: if `arr[i]` and `arr[j]` are already too far apart, no choice of `k` can rescue the triple, so the inner loop is skipped.

## Approach

1. Set `count` to 0.
2. Loop `i` over the array, and `j` over the indices after `i`.
3. If `|arr[i] - arr[j]| > a`, skip this pair with `continue`.
4. Otherwise loop `k` over the indices after `j` and compute `okJK` (the `b` rule) and `okIK` (the `c` rule).
5. When both hold, add one to `count`. Return `count` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [3, 0, 1, 1, 9, 7]`, `a = 7`, `b = 2`, `c = 3`.

- `i = 0` (3): from `j = 1` (0), `k` at the two 1s satisfies both rules: 2 triples. From `j = 2` (1), `k = 3` (1) works: 1 triple. `j = 4` (9) passes the `a` rule too, but its only `k` (7) is 4 away from 3, breaking the `c` rule.
- `i = 1` (0): from `j = 2` (1), `k = 3` (1) is within 2 of 1 and within 3 of 0: 1 triple.
- No other triple passes, so `count = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n³): three nested loops over the indices, at most n(n-1)(n-2)/6 checks.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters and flags.

## Pitfalls

- The indices must be strictly increasing; starting `j` at `i` or `k` at `j` counts the same element twice.
- Each rule uses `<=`, so a difference exactly equal to its limit is allowed.
- Do not forget the `i`–`k` rule with limit `c`; it is the one most often dropped.
- Triples are counted by position, so equal values at different indices count separately.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `arr` |
| `count` | number of good triples found so far |
| `i`, `j`, `k` | the three indices, with `i < j < k` |
| `okJK` | whether `arr[j]` and `arr[k]` are within `b` |
| `okIK` | whether `arr[i]` and `arr[k]` are within `c` |

narration.2: Remember the array length for the loop bounds.
narration.3: No good triples have been found yet.
narration.5: Fix the first index i; it needs two positions after it.
narration.6: Fix the second index j somewhere after i.
narration.7: Are arr[i] and arr[j] further apart than a?
narration.8: Then no k can make this triple good, so skip to the next j.
narration.10: Try every third index k after j.
narration.11: Check the rule between the second and third values against b.
narration.12: Check the rule between the first and third values against c.
narration.13: The a rule already holds, so both flags decide the triple.
narration.14: All three rules hold: count this triple.
narration.19: Every triple has been checked; return the total.
